title: The root `package.json` declares one runtime dependency and it is npm's security placeholder: `"coverage-v8": "0.0.1-security"`
body:
Found while working #5421 (reading the coverage lane's install log). Filed unassigned.

## What is there

`package.json` at the repo root, on `main` (`9f7d786bd`):

```json
"dependencies": {
  "coverage-v8": "0.0.1-security"
}
```

That is the entire `dependencies` block — the monorepo root otherwise declares everything under `devDependencies`, including the real one, `"@vitest/coverage-v8": "4.1.10"`.

`coverage-v8@0.0.1-security` is not a coverage tool. `0.0.1-security` is the version npm publishes under a name it has taken over after removing the original package; the tarball contains a README saying the name is held for security reasons and no code. It installs cleanly and does nothing, which is why it has gone unnoticed — every CI install prints it as a real-looking line:

```
dependencies:
+ coverage-v8 0.0.1-security
```

(visible in the install step of any `Test (coverage shard N/4)` job, e.g. [run 32397046084](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/32397046084)).

## Why it is worth removing rather than shrugging at

1. It is almost certainly a typo for `@vitest/coverage-v8` — someone ran the install without the scope. The scoped package is present and correct, so nothing is missing; this entry is pure residue.
2. It sits in **`dependencies`**, not `devDependencies`. A held name is not guaranteed to stay held forever, and the entry is pinned to an exact version so a re-release under a different version would not be picked up automatically — but the shape (an unscoped, single-word name in the root's only runtime dependency block) is the exact shape a supply-chain mistake takes, and nothing in the repo currently explains why it is there.
3. It occupies the root's `dependencies` block, so a reader looking for "what does the monorepo root depend on at runtime" gets one meaningless answer instead of the correct one (nothing).

## Suggested fix

Delete the `dependencies` block from the root `package.json` and refresh `pnpm-lock.yaml`. ⚠️ Touching the root lockfile has a wide blast radius while several agents hold worktrees, so this wants a quiet moment rather than a rider on another card — which is why it is filed rather than folded into #5421.
